The roadmap names the columns that failed to load instead of showing an empty board.

title: ATS Engine 0.17.0, Redesigned Marketing Pages, Template Gallery & Accessibility Fixes
summary: This release moves to ATS Engine 0.17.0, redesigns most marketing pages, adds a template gallery, and shows who built each release on the changelog. It also fixes keyboard, screen reader and contrast problems in the shared components that every VeriWorkly app uses. Some resumes will score differently with the new engine, so read the engine notes below.
added: The templates pages are now a gallery: three to four templates per row on desktop, two on a phone, with search, style and layout filters and a live count. A template page keeps its preview in view while the details scroll beside it.

The top of the changelog lists every contributor instead of the first ten, every release row has a fixed spot for its people, and every merged pull request is credited, with its author, to the right release.
improved: Upgraded @veriworkly/ats-engine from 0.16.0 to 0.17.0 across server, site, Studio and docs. Scores can change for the same resume: "Till now", "onwards" and "bis heute" read as a current role, the right to work is compared by country, expired or in-progress certifications are partial, and a degree requirement that says "or related field" no longer accepts years of work instead of the degree. Deploy the rebuilt private scoring policy with this release.

A job posting from a URL is read up to 20,000 characters instead of 12,000. An AI analysis that comes back completely empty now counts as no answer and is tried again, and when retries are on the AI waits between tries.

More resumes are read correctly: PDFs with Chinese, Japanese or Korean fonts, files with old-style line breaks, and a name followed by a job title on the first line. Hebrew and Arabic resumes no longer lose 10 points for direction marks, and a verb such as "Reacted" no longer counts as the skill React.

Every marketing page except the landing page, pricing, roadmap, style guide, brand kit and the affiliate and ambassador pages has a new design on one shared layout. The ATS checker page shows two plans, and the About page hides the affiliate and ambassador links while those programs are off.
Dialogs announce their title, keep focus when the page behind them updates, open above the navbar, and close one at a time with Escape. On a phone, swipe a dialog down to close it.
Dropdown menus work with the arrow keys, Home, End and typing a letter, and Escape returns focus to the menu button. Tooltips appear above dialogs, stay open while hovered, and close with Escape.
The mobile menu no longer lets Tab reach its links while closed or the page behind it while open. FAQ answers stay searchable with Ctrl+F in browsers that support it.
Error red is a little darker in light mode and the footer text is easier to read, so both meet the 4.5:1 contrast minimum. Native scrollbars, dropdown lists and date pickers now follow dark mode.
Buttons shrink slightly when pressed and keyboard focus rings on buttons and links are solid blue.
fixed: Styles passed to a button made with asChild were dropped. They now apply, so about 20 buttons (blog and docs calls to action, Studio login, portfolio error pages, the main button in the mobile menu) look as designed.
The Security page no longer claims encrypted local storage, AES-256, TLS 1.3 or a 24-hour response time, which the code does not back up.
The Compare pages read prices and feature tables from one set of competitor data. The old copy had wrong prices for Novoresume and Zety.

Dialogs, tooltips and checkboxes were missing their animations. A checkbox ignored its starting value. The first click on the theme button did nothing on a system already set to dark. Icon-only links and two form controls had no names for screen readers.
Text fields use 16px text on phones so iPhones no longer zoom in, and blog posts no longer scroll sideways on a phone.
Synced release notes no longer leak horizontal rules, the Pull Requests list or the Full Changelog link into the bullets, and the intro paragraph is kept as the summary.

title: ATS Engine 0.16.0, Seniority Rows & Keyword Stuffing Spread Over a Few Skills
summary: This release moves the server, site and Studio to @veriworkly/ats-engine 0.16.0 (from 0.14.0). The ATS checker now catches keyword stuffing that names a few skills again and again on one line. A job posting titled with a level, such as "Senior Backend Engineer", gets a seniority row in the requirements table. A resume that copies one bullet into three or four roles is no longer marked as keyword stuffing, so some resumes gain 10 points.
improved: Upgraded @veriworkly/ats-engine from 0.14.0 to 0.16.0 across server, site, Studio and docs.

A line that names a few skills again and again, such as "Keywords: Python Kubernetes AWS Docker Go Kafka" written four times, is now keyword stuffing: terms named three times or more each, totalling 10 words or more and half the line. With the default policy, an invented resume with that line falls from 92 to 82. The job match is unchanged.

A job posting titled with a level, such as "Senior Backend Engineer", gets a first row in the requirements table with kind "seniority", judged by the resume's latest title and years. The score does not change.

A sentence bullet copied word for word once into each of three or four roles is no longer keyword stuffing: 46 of 3,000 generated resumes gain 10 points. Five or more roles still count. The default policy gains seniority levels, so a private policy must be rebuilt.
The policy JSON Schema is strict, a job posting saved as .xhtml is read as a web page, and the MCP server takes a region for explain_rule.
The docs reference pages and changelog are regenerated for 0.16.0, and the integrity and job matching pages describe the new behaviour.

title: ATS Engine 0.14.0, Job URLs & Upload Reliability
summary: This release moves the server, site and Studio to @veriworkly/ats-engine 0.14.0 and fixes the ATS checker's server side. "Analyze from a job URL" works again, one slow upload no longer fails the uploads behind it, and a Redis outage no longer hangs every request. The checker now reads hidden text in a PDF or Word file more precisely: white keywords no longer count, and visible skills are no longer dropped because a hidden line repeats them.
improved: Upgraded @veriworkly/ats-engine from 0.11.0 to 0.14.0 across server, site and Studio.

Hidden text in a PDF or Word file is set aside only where the extracted text holds it, and white text after visible text is cut from that line: on 6,000 generated resumes, hidden-only skills counted fell from 902 to 14 and visible skills lost from 1,267 to 43.
Job postings saved as UTF-16 or Windows-1252 are read correctly.
The docs and the /ats-engine page read bundle sizes from the installed engine.
fixed: "Analyze from a job URL" failed for every address on Node 20 and later; it works again, with a 15-second limit on the whole fetch.
One slow or crashing upload no longer fails the uploads queued behind it, and an upload the server refuses for its own reasons no longer uses up a scan.
A file over 5 MB says it is too large instead of "Internal server error", and a long PDF no longer fails because a layout count ran past its limit.
During a Redis outage, requests fall back at once instead of hanging.
The docs preview images answer "not found" for a missing page, and every preview-image route runs on Node.
security: The job-URL fetcher refuses IPv6 addresses that carry an internal IPv4 address (mapped, compatible and NAT64 forms).
The anonymous scan quota and rate limits count an IPv6 /64 as one client, and the upload route accepts no extra form fields.

title: ATS Engine Docs, Developer Page & Engine 0.11.0
summary: This release gives the open-source ATS engine its own documentation at docs.veriworkly.com/ats-engine and a developer page at veriworkly.com/ats-engine, and moves the server, site and Studio to @veriworkly/ats-engine 0.11.0. Since 3.26.0 the checker reads French CVs and UK resumes in their own conventions, no longer judges a resume in a language without a pack by English writing rules, judges work authorisation, sponsorship and clearances more carefully, redacts more before the AI deep analysis, and caps what a crafted PDF or Word upload can cost.
added: ATS Engine documentation: a new docs tree at docs.veriworkly.com/ats-engine with a quick start, concepts, guides for Node.js, Next.js, the edge and the browser, the CLI, the GitHub Action, the MCP server, and a reference generated from the installed engine.

ATS Engine developer page: /ats-engine on the marketing site, with an in-browser demo that scores invented sample resumes with the real engine, the four ways to run it, runtimes, bundle sizes, benchmarks and the hosted API's quotas.
French and UK resumes: French CVs are read in French, and a resume with a +44 number is read in UK conventions (day-first dates, GCSEs, HNDs, PGCEs).
Six developer FAQ entries about the ATS engine, and links to it from the footer, the ATS checker, the features page, llms.txt and agent.json.
improved: Upgraded @veriworkly/ats-engine from 0.5.0 to 0.10.0 and then 0.11.0 across server, site and Studio; reading fixes from 0.6 to 0.9 improve recovered fields and scores for the same file.
A resume in a language the engine has no pack for no longer gets the English-only writing checks.

Job matching: a posting that offers sponsorship no longer rules a candidate out, a clearance's level is read where the posting names it, UK clearances (BPSS, CTC, SC, DV) are compared by level, and British and American spellings match each other.
Docs CI type-checks every ATS Engine code sample and fails if the generated reference pages fall behind the installed engine.
Re-checked Kickresume, Novorésumé and Enhancv pricing in the comparison matrix, and linked the four career guides from the blog's front page.
fixed: Uploads: PDF reading stops after 100 pages, a DOCX's headers and footers share one 2 MB budget, and PDF images are decoded a page at a time, so a padded or image-heavy file can no longer tie up the checker.

Integrity checks: keyword stuffing no longer fires on honest compact resumes or academic publications, and a quoted prompt-injection example in a security engineer's resume is no longer flagged, while a quoted screener prompt still is.
Old unprefixed template URLs such as /templates/executive-clarity now redirect permanently to their current pages instead of serving soft 404s, and /stats pages after the first are no longer indexed.
security: AI deep analysis redacts more before the resume reaches the model: local and exit-prefixed phone numbers, a second phone number, email addresses with accented letters or an apostrophe, and two-character Chinese or Korean names; nothing past the 50,000-character cut is sent.

title: Next.js 16.3.8 Security Patch, Dependency Advisories Cleared & Leaner Overrides
summary: This release patches a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Next.js, in the code every VeriWorkly app uses to draw its link-preview images, and closes every other dependency advisory that has an upstream fix: npm audit goes from 21 findings (1 critical) to 5, all in one lint-only package that never ships. Dependencies are also updated within their current major versions, and the root dependency overrides are trimmed to the ones that still do something.
improved: Updated Prisma to 7.10.0.
Updated Studio's document export libraries: @react-pdf/renderer to 4.9.0 and docx to 9.8.1. Resume PDFs pass the existing PDF parity tests unchanged.
Updated other packages within their current major versions, including the AWS SDK, Dodo Payments, mammoth, pg, Resend, lucide-react, libphonenumber-js and Prettier.
Better Auth stays on 1.6.x: 1.7 requires a database migration and will ship separately.
The blog and docs now pin exactly the same fumadocs versions, and the root overrides keep a single copy of fumadocs for every package that depends on it.

Removed overrides for packages no longer in the dependency tree (hono, @hono/node-server, better-sqlite3), one that had no effect (valibot), and nested entries that repeated top-level rules. The installed dependency tree is unchanged.
The local setup guide and README now state the npm version the repository requires: 11 or higher.
fixed: The site now declares tsx, which its build scripts use. Before, the site build only worked because the server happened to install it.
Corrected the tech stack description in veriworkly.md: Playwright is a Studio development dependency for browser tests, and no export path uses a headless browser.
security: Upgraded Next.js and eslint-config-next from 16.3.5 to 16.3.8 across the site, Studio, portfolio, blog and docs. This fixes remote code execution in next/og ImageResponse (GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j), which every app uses for its social preview images, along with a server-side request forgery in image optimization and cache-poisoning issues in statically generated pages.

Upgraded Nodemailer from 9.1.1 to 10.0.14 on the server. 9.x has no patched release. This fixes SMTP credentials leaking across transports through a shared DNS cache (GHSA-6vj9-mwq6-2f5v) and four address-parser flaws: three denial-of-service attacks (GHSA-prgh-xp8r-p3m5, GHSA-v53p-9fqp-m79j, GHSA-8vvx-rff5-p5rq) and a malformed envelope recipient (GHSA-g57g-f23g-4646).

Upgraded Express to 4.22.3, which brings qs 6.16 and fixes a request-parsing array-limit bypass and denial of service (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx, GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g), and Multer to 2.4.0, which fixes a denial of service through aborted uploads (GHSA-3pph-fpjx-jg34).

Corrected root overrides that were pinning vulnerable versions: fast-uri is now 3.1.8, fixing seven host-confusion and server-side request forgery advisories (the previous 3.1.7 override had never actually applied), and body-parser is now 1.20.8.
Overrode mysql2 to 3.24.5 and deepmerge-ts to 8.0.2. Prisma 7 pins vulnerable versions of both, including a plaintext credential leak in mysql2 (GHSA-3f6p-5ww8-9rcr).

Updated @xmldom/xmldom to 0.8.15, used when reading uploaded Word documents. This fixes XML injection and quadratic-time parsing advisories. Also updated nanoid, brace-expansion, and Vitest (a path traversal in test tooling, GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9).

title: Requirement-by-Requirement Matching, Resume Integrity Checks & an Open-Source ATS Engine
summary: This release changes how the ATS checker reads and scores a resume. Every requirement in a job posting is now checked against your resume one by one, the checker catches the hidden-text and keyword tricks that get resumes rejected, and our resume templates now come through ATS text extraction intact. The engine behind all of it is now open source and published on npm as @veriworkly/ats-engine, so anyone can see exactly how a resume is read and scored.
added: Requirement-by-requirement matching: paste a job posting and each requirement is marked Met, Partly met, Not shown, or Answer in the application (for things a resume cannot settle, such as the right to work), together with the lines from your resume it relied on.

Integrity checks for white or tiny text, text hidden in PDF and Word files, invisible and look-alike characters, instructions written for AI screeners, a pasted job posting, and keywords repeated far beyond normal use. They only lower the score when something is found: an honest resume scores exactly as if these checks did not exist.
German and Hindi support: resumes and job postings in German and Hindi are read in their own language, with US, German and Indian conventions for phone numbers, date order and qualifications.
The ATS engine is open source: @veriworkly/ats-engine is published on npm under the MIT license with build provenance, and developed in its own repository at github.com/VeriWorkly/ats-engine.
improved: Studio's ATS workspace now sends your resume as structured data instead of having it re-read from a PDF, so it is scored exactly as you wrote it.

Resume templates are ATS-safe: section titles were spaced so widely that PDF readers split them into single letters and an ATS found no Experience section. Spacing is now capped on every template, and the headline sits under your name instead of beside it, where it was being read as part of the name.

More resumes are read correctly, including dates written with a day (15 March 2020), headings in sentence case (Education and certifications), job titles that begin with a section word (Education Coordinator), and titles written as Data Scientist @ Netflix.

Requirement matching is smarter: a bachelor's degree or 4 years of experience is met by either one, 3 to 5 years asks for 3, a list of languages is read as a list, and a state code such as Boston, MA is no longer mistaken for a master's degree.

AI analysis is more private: your name, email and phone number are removed before your resume is sent to the AI model, and anything the model returns must actually appear in your resume before it is shown.
The server, site and Studio now use the published engine instead of keeping their own copies of the same logic, and the API documentation describes the new report fields.
fixed: A phone number followed by a line that starts with digits no longer swallows those digits.
Lines beginning with .NET are no longer mistaken for bullet points.
White text in dark table cells, phone numbers in Arabic and Hebrew resumes, and Greek letters in scientific terms such as TNFα are no longer flagged as hidden or suspicious.
breaking: ATS scores change: the same resume and job posting will usually score differently than on 3.24.x. Scoring now follows a published rubric, a check with nothing to judge is left out instead of being counted as a pass, and a resume caught gaming the screener can no longer earn a strong verdict from its job match alone.
security: Word uploads are measured exactly the way the document reader opens them, so a small file built to expand into gigabytes (a zip bomb) is refused before it is ever unpacked.
Resumes, job postings and AI responses are processed in linear time even when they are deliberately crafted to be slow, closing several ways a single upload could tie up the server.

title: Resend API Email Integration, Connection-Pooled SMTP & OAuth Cancellation Redirect Fix
summary: This release adds native Resend transactional email integration via its REST API, hardens the SMTP transport with connection pooling and socket timeouts, and fixes a Better Auth redirect issue where cancelling social login sent users to raw API JSON instead of the Studio login screen.
added: Native Resend email provider support via the official SDK and RESEND_API_KEY for fast, firewall-resilient transactional email delivery over HTTPS.
Connection pooling, keepalive, and socket timeouts for Nodemailer SMTP transport to prevent socket exhaustion and timeouts on relays.
Dedicated unit test suites covering Resend dispatch, error handling, and production runtime startup validation.
improved: Updated validateAuthRuntimeConfig to accept both resend and smtp as valid production email providers.
Replaced direct window object calls in Studio SocialAuth with idiomatic Next.js useSearchParams and site config URLs.
Updated environment documentation across .env.example, .env.docker.example, compose.yaml, and operations docs.
fixed: Fixed Better Auth OAuth cancellation fallback redirecting to root API JSON instead of the Studio login page with an informative toast.
Fixed query parameter persistence on the Studio login page by cleaning error params from browser history after acknowledgement.

summary: This release upgrades Next.js to 16.3.5 across all frontend apps to patch a critical remote code execution vulnerability, updates React to 19.3.0, and updates Sharp to 0.35.4. We also removed redundant React and Sharp overrides from the root package configuration, updated Multer and Nodemailer to patched versions, added offline safety to the changelog static export, and extracted the ATS scoring and parsing engine into a dedicated workspace package.
added: Extracted ATS scoring, tokenizer, and parsing rules into a shared @veriworkly/ats-engine package consumed by the server and frontend applications.
Added ATS AI processing service with strict schema formatting, grounding validation, and automated repair routines.
Added generate script in root package.json for building docs API routes.
improved: Upgraded Next.js and eslint-config-next from 16.2.12 to 16.3.5 across apps/site, apps/studio, apps/portfolio, apps/blog-platform, and apps/docs-platform.
Upgraded React and react-dom to 19.3.0 across all frontend applications.
Removed root package overrides for React, react-dom, and Sharp, allowing npm workspace hoisting to resolve deduplicated copies directly.
Updated veriworkly.md tech stack documentation to reference Next.js 16.3.5 and React 19.3.0.
fixed: Resolved static build failure in apps/site when prerendering changelog release pages without an active backend server.
Broke circular module dependency between template registry and template-details in apps/portfolio.
Improved private policy error reporting and path resolution in apps/server.
security: Patched critical remote code execution vulnerability on Windows-hosted servers (GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36) and Image Optimization API flaw (GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4) by upgrading Next.js to 16.3.5.
Patched libheif vulnerabilities (GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c) by updating Sharp to 0.35.4.
Updated multer to 2.3.0 in apps/server to patch multipart parsing denial-of-service vulnerabilities.
Updated nodemailer to 9.1.1 in apps/server to patch recipient-domain validation and address-parser denial-of-service flaws.
Updated root overrides for fast-uri to 3.1.7 and js-yaml to 4.3.2 to remediate upstream advisories.

title: ATS Engine Rebuild, Claims Accuracy Audit, Account Deletion & Legal Remediation
summary: This patch release rebuilds the ATS parsing engine with layout detection and a worker extraction pool, adds self-service account deletion, and remediates a full audit of every public claim on the marketing site against the code that has to honour it. Marketing copy that promised features which did not exist has been removed or labelled as forthcoming, the security page has been rebuilt from what the repository can actually prove, and the Terms and Privacy Policy have been given the structural sections they were missing.
added: AtsResumeParseService with bounding-box layout detection, identifying multi-column resumes and ruled table grids that scramble text extraction order
Worker-based PDF and DOCX stream extraction via ExtractPool, with contact extraction, section segmentation, and keyword tokenization
Separate, more generous ATS extraction quota (3 anonymous, 6 free account, 300 paid) so uploading a file no longer consumes a scan from the smaller scan budget
ParsedView component in the ATS scanner exposing the raw parsed stream, detected sections, and linear reading flow the engine actually sees
Self-service account deletion from the Studio profile page, with a Danger Zone card and a type-your-email confirmation modal listing exactly what is destroyed
denyApiKeyAuth middleware, restricting irreversible whole-account actions to session-authenticated requests from first-party origins
Notice-and-takedown section in the Terms of Service with a reporting address, required notice contents, acknowledgement and decision timelines, a counter-notice route, and a repeat-infringer policy
Named Grievance Officer and Data Protection Contact published in both the Terms and the Privacy Policy, with a dedicated email address and postal address
Complete subprocessor table in the Privacy Policy naming every third party, what personal data each receives, its processing region, and the transfer mechanism relied on
Breach-notification commitment, concrete data retention periods, and the right to complain to a supervisory authority in the Privacy Policy
TRADEMARK.md and LICENSING.md at the repository root, stating precisely what the MIT licence covers and what it does not
Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off requirement in CONTRIBUTING.md
Safe-harbour clause for good-faith security research in SECURITY.md and on the security page
Skip-to-content link in AppShell, satisfying WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (Level A), which had no implementation anywhere in the application
Person entity in JSON-LD with a stable @id, sameAs, jobTitle, and knowsAbout, plus a root WebSite node and @id graph linking across all schemas

Claims contract test suite asserting cross-file agreement between marketing copy and the server: template IDs resolve, compare routes exist, the portfolio model matches enforcement, credit-pack expiry is stated, and ATS preview labels match the engine
Prisma migration removing TRIALING from the SubscriptionStatus enum
improved: ATS checker landing and scan pages rebuilt from monolithic files into domain-driven modules under components/tool, components/hero, and components/guide
Navbar decomposed into LogoPill, DesktopNav, ActionsPill, and MobileMenu, with useMounted and useScrolled layout hooks
Features, how-it-works, security, compare, contact, and FAQ pages modularized into composable sections with decoupled static datasets
Changelog and GitHub services broken out of monolithic files into services/github and services/changelog subfolders with distinct responsibilities
Navbar now links Features, How It Works, and Compare, which previously had no header link from anywhere on the site
check-design-tokens now fails the build when a design token mapped in no @theme block is used as a utility class, rather than only printing a warning
Portfolio publishing model stated identically across every surface: Signal and Atelier free with a badge, Nimbus and Cipher on a paid plan, all qualified as opening at launch
Security page claims rebuilt from what the repository can prove, with third-party compliance attributed to the provider rather than asserted directly
JSON-LD offers consolidated onto the pricing page, with offerCount and price bounds derived from a single array rather than hardcoded alongside it
AccordionTrigger accepts a configurable heading level, so FAQ questions sit at the correct depth per page instead of a hard-coded h3
fixed: Root 404 boundary was a copy of the error boundary: its primary button called an undefined reset(), throwing a TypeError on every unmatched URL outside the marketing route group
DELETE /users/me was reachable with any API key holding the user:write scope, the same scope used to rename an account, allowing an integration token to irreversibly destroy an entire account

Account deletion dropped the local subscription record without cancelling at the payment provider, which would have left users charged for an account that no longer existed; deletion is now blocked while a subscription would renew
Account deletion removed R2 storage objects before the database transaction, so a failed transaction left an intact account whose uploaded images had silently vanished
Deleting an account left the user's published portfolio served from cache; the subdomain is now captured before deletion and its caches invalidated
removeWatermark arrived inside the client-supplied portfolio payload and was persisted verbatim, without being checked against the watermark_removal entitlement
text-muted-foreground was mapped into no @theme block, so 36 usages in apps/site and 98 in apps/studio emitted no CSS and rendered uncoloured
LegalSections rendered a second main landmark inside AppShell's, giving the privacy and terms pages two main regions for screen-reader navigation
Contact form submissions logged the sender's name, email, and subject, exceeding the server-log contents disclosed in the Privacy Policy

llms.txt advertised three /compare routes that hard-404 under dynamicParams = false while omitting three that exist, and listed every resume template ID without its resume- prefix, breaking all seven template links
FAQPage structured data was duplicated verbatim between /faq and /ats-checker, and seven Offer nodes shipped into the head of every route including /privacy and /terms
The /faq page had no h2 elements in its own content, leaving every question as an orphaned h3 beneath the page h1; the footer emitted an h2 to h4 skip on every page
hreflang emitted only en-US, region-locking an India-based service with a global English-speaking audience; single-language sites should emit none
noIndex pages emitted a canonical URL, and the 404 boundaries pointed theirs at /404 and /roadmap/404, routes that do not exist
Homepage HowTo structured data used an invalid HowToSupply type for estimatedCost, and two of four steps carried neither position nor url
Unguarded ev.touches[0] in use-mouse-position-ref threw when the touch list was empty
A Suspense boundary on the pricing page wrapped a component that awaited nothing, rendering a second copy of a large client tree that never displayed
Templates hero fan selected the first three catalog entries, which are all portfolios, cropping landscape screenshots into a portrait paper frame
manifest.json declared the standard icons as maskable, which Android crops to a safe zone and would clip on home screens
breaking: Free trials have been removed from all plans. Creator Pro monthly previously applied an automatic 7-day trial for first-time subscribers; no plan now carries one, and the TRIALING subscription status has been removed from the schema. No subscription was ever created under the trial, so no existing records are affected.
security: Account deletion is now session-only. DELETE /users/me previously accepted any API key holding user:write, the same scope required to rename an account, which put a long-lived integration token one call away from irreversibly destroying every document, portfolio, credit, and payout record on the account

Published portfolio snapshots now record the server's own watermark decision rather than the client-supplied removeWatermark flag, which was persisted without being checked against the watermark_removal entitlement
Contact form logging no longer records submitter identity fields, aligning server logs with what the Privacy Policy discloses

The security page no longer asserts LocalStorage encryption, AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3, zero logging, cryptographic purge, or WASM/Canvas rendering, none of which the repository implements or can verify; a stated but unsupported security guarantee is worse than no claim
Removed the advertised bug bounty and 24-hour SLA guarantee, neither of which existed, and added a safe-harbour clause so good-faith researchers have stated authorisation
